# Workflows

Flat folder (GitHub requirement), organized by prefix.

Source of truth: [`docs/DESIGN.md` — sections 3, 4 and 15](../../docs/DESIGN.md#4-cicd) (names in [section 1](../../docs/DESIGN.md#workflows)).

## Local rules

- **Reusable** (`ci-`, `deploy-`, `release-`): only `on: workflow_call`, so they don't run on every commit here. Called by the projects' `ci.yml`, pinned by SHA.
- **This repository's own**: prefix `self-` (e.g. `self-validate-marketplace.yml`, `self-lint.yml`, `self-test-features.yml`, `self-publish-features.yml`, `self-cleanup-tests.yml`).
- `self-shared-database.yml`: manual (`workflow_dispatch`) start/stop/status of the shared platform's Cloud SQL instance, on `main` only; uses the repository secrets `GCP_SHARED_PROJECT_ID`, `GCP_SHARED_WIF_PROVIDER` and `GCP_SHARED_SWITCH_ACCOUNT`.
- `ci-go.yml`: reusable check of one Go component (one module in one folder). Inputs `working-directory` (the module's folder, relative to the repository root) and `go-version` (`major.minor`), both required. Steps: checkout, set up Go (no cache), `gofmt -l` (fails and lists the files when one is not formatted), `go vet ./...`, `go test ./...`, `go build ./...`. Permission `contents: read`; no secrets. A project's `ci.yml` calls it once per component, pinned by commit SHA.
- `self-test-ci-go.yml`: tests `ci-go.yml` before a project uses it. On pull requests that change `ci-go.yml`, this file or `.github/testdata/ci-go/**`, it calls `ci-go.yml` on the fixture module in `.github/testdata/ci-go` (the Go starting point of `aleogr-stack-go`, its three templates rendered for a component `sample`: a small standard-library HTTP server with one test per handler) with Go `1.27`.
- `deploy-cloud-run.yml`: reusable deploy of one component to its existing Cloud Run service. It builds the image from the component's folder, pushes it to Artifact Registry as `<image>:<commit SHA>`, then runs `gcloud run services update <service> --image=<image>@sha256:<digest>` with the digest the push returned (refused unless it is `sha256:` and 64 hex characters). That is the only change it makes to the service: it never creates one, never changes who may reach it; a missing service fails. Steps: mask the identifiers and validate the inputs (first step, before anything else), checkout, `google-github-actions/auth` (workload identity federation, no key), `docker/login-action` on `<region>-docker.pkg.dev`, `docker/setup-buildx-action` (its binary not cached), `docker/build-push-action` (no job summary, no build-record artifact, no check annotations: `DOCKER_BUILD_SUMMARY`, `DOCKER_BUILD_RECORD_UPLOAD` and `DOCKER_BUILD_CHECKS_ANNOTATIONS` are `false`, since a summary or an artifact is not redacted and would carry the registry path; no provenance or SBOM, so the digest is the image's own), `google-github-actions/setup-gcloud`, the update. One job (permissions repeated on it), 20 minutes at most, one deploy at a time per service (`concurrency: deploy-<service>`, never cancelled).
  - Inputs, all required strings: `working-directory` (the component's folder, holding its `Dockerfile`: matches `^[A-Za-z0-9_-][A-Za-z0-9._/-]*$` and has no `..` segment, so it is never `.`, absolute or outside the repository, and the credentials file that `auth` writes at the workspace root is outside the build context), `service` and `image-name` (each `^[a-z][a-z0-9-]{0,48}$`), `region` (`^[a-z]+-[a-z]+[0-9]{1,2}$`). The first step refuses an input that does not match with one error naming the input, never its value. Secrets, all required: `project-id`, `workload-identity-provider` (full path, `projects/<number>/locations/global/workloadIdentityPools/<pool>/providers/<provider>`), `service-account` (the CI account), `image-path` (`<region>-docker.pkg.dev/<project>/<repository>`); the image is `<image-path>/<image-name>`. No outputs. A project's `ci.yml` passes the four identifiers as `secrets:` from its repository secrets `GCP_PROJECT_ID`, `GCP_WIF_PROVIDER`, `GCP_CI_ACCOUNT` and `GCP_IMAGE_PATH` (for example `project-id: ${{ secrets.GCP_PROJECT_ID }}`), never `secrets: inherit`, and writes `region` as a literal (the region is in the public declaration).
  - Masking: the identifiers arrive as secrets, which the runner masks from the job's start; the first step also registers `::add-mask::` for the project id, the service account, the provider path, the image path and the project number (read from the provider path), so later steps and the URL `gcloud` prints show `***`. Values reach scripts only through `env`. GitHub masks a repository secret in every log and does not give it to a pull request from a fork; that the four arrive masked in the called workflow's log is still to be confirmed by the first real run.
  - The caller must: call it from a job that runs only on `push` to the default branch, pinned by commit SHA; grant that job `permissions: contents: read, id-token: write` (a called workflow cannot raise them); have a provider whose condition accepts this workflow's `job_workflow_ref`; and give the CI account `roles/run.developer` on the service, `roles/iam.serviceAccountUser` on the service's own account, and push access (`roles/artifactregistry.writer`, which includes reading) on the image repository.
- `self-test-deploy-cloud-run.yml`: on pull requests that change `deploy-cloud-run.yml`, this file or `.github/testdata/deploy-cloud-run/**`, runs `.github/testdata/deploy-cloud-run/check.sh` on `deploy-cloud-run.yml`. The check parses the YAML with the runner's system Python and PyYAML (`/usr/bin/python3`, Ubuntu's `python3-yaml`; if it is missing the check fails, it never skips) and refuses duplicate keys, anchors and aliases.
  - It proves, of the file's text: `workflow_call` is the only trigger, with exactly the four inputs and the four secrets; no other privileged trigger, no create, no change of who may reach the service, no `secrets: inherit`, no whole-context dump; `secrets` is read only by the four names, and no identifier is an input; one job with exactly the expected keys and permissions; exactly the eight expected steps in order, each action pinned by a 40-character SHA with its version in a comment, no `if`, `continue-on-error` or `shell` on any step; each action step's `id`, `with` and `env` exactly as reviewed (the login's registry and password, auth's provider and account, the build's context, tags, provenance and SBOM; no other key), so the summary, build-record and annotations are off and Buildx is not cached; no `${{ }}`, line continuation or empty `add-mask` in a script, and one `gcloud` in all scripts; the two scripts and their `env` exactly as reviewed (so the digest test precedes the update, which is the last command).
  - It does not prove anything about run time: that the identifiers arrive masked, that the actions' defaults and switches behave as their READMEs say, that a SHA is the version its comment names, or anything about the caller (that its job runs only on `push` to the default branch). A change to either script changes the check in the same pull request.
  - It is advisory unless the repository makes it a required status check. The deploy itself needs a cloud and is not run here.
- `self-test-skills.yml`: on pull requests that change `.claude-plugin/**` or this file, runs the unit tests of the plugins' commands (`python3 -m unittest discover -s .claude-plugin/tests/unit`: the copies of `aleogr_common.py` are byte-identical, the read-only runner refuses every command that is not a read before running it) and `.claude-plugin/tests/run-direct.sh`, every scenario of a converted skill in the direct mode of `run.sh` (no model: the plugin's command against the fake CLIs); a scenario whose skill is not converted is counted, not run. Permission `contents: read`; no secrets; the runner's system Python 3, standard library only. It is advisory unless the repository makes it a required status check.
- Action references (`uses:`) are pinned by full commit SHA with the version in a comment; `.github/dependabot.yml` proposes their updates weekly.
- Versioning by prefixed tags: `workflows-v1`, `workflows-v2`...
- Secrets received explicitly by name; **never** `secrets: inherit`.
- Logs of public workflows are public: **no workflow prints variables or secrets**.

> Warning: never create `.github/README.md` — it would replace the profile README.
